title: John Chrysostom on Zechariah 9:9
body: “Wonderful! How great is the tyranny of gluttony, how great the fickleness of men's minds! No longer do they vindicate the Law, no longer do they care for the violation of the Sabbath, no longer are they zealous for God; all such considerations are thrown aside, when their bellies have been filled; He was a prophet in their eyes, and they were about to choose Him for a king.”
author: John Chrysostom, Homilies on John and Hebrews

title: John Chrysostom on Zechariah 9:9
body: “But how, after not walking openly in Jewry, and retiring into the wilderness, doth He again enter openly? Having quenched their anger by retiring, He cometh to them when they were stilled.”
author: John Chrysostom, Homilies on John and Hebrews

title: John Chrysostom on Zechariah 12:10
body: “Neither was he content with this, but added, "according to the Scriptures:" hereby both again making his argument credible, and intimating what kind of death he was speaking of: since it is the death of the body which the Scriptures everywhere proclaim. For, "they pierced My hands and My feet," (Ps.”
author: John Chrysostom, Homilies on the Epistles to the Corinthians

title: John Chrysostom on Zechariah 12:10
body: “Seest thou how strong a thing is truth? By means of the very things which are the objects of their zeal, prophecy is fulfilled, for by occasion of those things, this plain prediction, unconnected with them, receives its accomplishment.”
author: John Chrysostom, Homilies on John and Hebrews
